summary.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, a scene linked with readiness. Today’s simplified 备 commonly means “prepare” or “ready.”

formation.text: The traditional graph 備 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 depicts an arrow container and is also assigned a sound role. Together, they have been interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, a scene linked to preparedness. The component’s proposed sound role has a Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison, though the component’s pronunciation is not independently documented here. 备 is the officially adopted simplified form corresponding to 備.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the interpreted carrying scene associated with preparedness.

In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. Its proposed sound role is supported by a Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison, though an independent reading for 𤰈 is unavailable here.

sound_limitation.text: The Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison is supplied for both 𤰈 and 備, but no independent character-specific historical reading for 𤰈 was retrieved to verify the component’s pronunciation or sound role.

sound.text: The proposed component reading *bɯɡ and 備 *brɯɡs share the initial *b and rhyme material, with an added final *s in 備; this comparison is supplied in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system.

components.text: 备 is officially listed as the simplified form corresponding to 備. A proposed derivation through variant 俻 by deleting 亻 is not established by the official scheme.

history.text: 備 is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, though its earliest appearance is not dated in the cited accounts.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and described as a changed form of seal-script 𤰈. Bronze forms also show its lower part changed to 用, tentatively interpreted as a sound element; a complete dated sequence is not established.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not establish it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 reportedly writes 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match between that name and 𤰈.

備 appears with glosses including prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: A received dictionary gloss is 慎也, “cautious” or “careful”; this does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a whole-graph loan for 箙, “quiver”: 備 was reused to write a different word on a proposed sound resemblance, rather than because “prepare” developed into “quiver.” The resemblance is not independently demonstrated, and the pictured object’s original name is unresolved.

overview.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, a scene linked with being equipped and ready. The picture does not prove the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 备 is the simplified form and commonly means “prepare” or “ready.”
